metric_contract.original_recall_at_k: First gold URL at a chunk position <= k: a hit rate, not multi-gold recall.
metric_contract.original_ndcg_at_10: 1/log2(1+first gold chunk rank), zero after 10; only first hit contributes; implicit IDCG=1.
metric_contract.original_mrr: Reciprocal first gold chunk rank in complete stored ranking (not MRR@10).
metric_contract.final_gold_page_hit: G: gold page in actual final_urls; no claim of content support or compliance with a prespecified source policy.
metric_contract.distinct_page_metrics: Stable unique URL order; binary relevance; IDCG from ALL frozen gold pages, including unretrieved ones. Ten pages and ten chunks are different budgets.
metric_contract.url_matching: Exact string after outer whitespace stripping, matching the frozen original scorer; no URL canonicalization.
metric_contract.missing_annotation: Hard error or flagged unmatched record; never treated as irrelevant.
metric_contract.query_normalization: Only named normalization log is joined by stable qid despite changed question text; tracked explicitly.

e0_findings.detail: Seven changed queries per mode fail the original (qid, question) annotation join and are scored zero. All released rewritten query texts are reproduced by generate_normalized_questions.py. Stable qid with validated rewrite recovers their original gold; see normalization_join_diagnosis.csv and corrected_normalization_metrics.csv.

iso78 and original78 slice of exp155 are different frozen outputs; see cross_run_comparison.csv. Historical run IDs, API response IDs and timestamps are absent. Retain both with source file hashes; no repeated-run distribution can be inferred.
ablation_no_dedup retains reranking; ablation_base_no_dedup removes cap without reranking. Compare their named configurations, not the generic NoDedup label.
Full-list, top-10, and top-4 transition tables are provided separately. Both-missing is cutoff dependent; final hit equality can conceal offsetting losses and rescues.
Depth24 uses pool100, whereas pool24 reranks the post-cap pool from 24 retrieved chunks. The unreranked tail is appended by implementation. These are not the same setting.
Prior examples q58 (5->12) and q9 (8->12) are ranking degradations with no top-4 loss. true_top4_transitions.csv enumerates actual delivered gold-page losses/rescues.

The LLM sees a candidate list and assigns each chunk a 0-2 score (500 characters each); stable sorting yields order. Describe as joint-context ordinal chunk scoring, not direct list permutation. temperature=0; request failures silently return all-zero scores in historical code.

limitations: Only ranking/final URLs are in compact retrieval logs; no candidate IDs, chunk IDs, raw candidate URLs, final text, or raw model responses. Earlier-stage plots and content utility cannot be independently rebuilt from these logs.
URL-level candidate equality cannot establish identical chunk-level candidate sets.
Original and expanded questions use only designated NCI pages; the expansion includes original questions and source-conditioned construction, not independent external validation.
All present evaluation labels are automatic. No human U, acceptable multi-source labels, clinical validation, or independent E1/E2 test is present.
Four chunks is not a fixed tokenizer-measured token budget. Stored latency is historical wall time; hardware/model revision/API cost metadata are incomplete.
Recorded configuration tables can omit modes present in merged logs. File hashes identify frozen artifacts, not historical model snapshots or a missing run manifest.
Question and page-cluster bootstrap intervals are descriptive sensitivity analyses; few page groups and unadjusted multiple comparisons limit inferential claims.
